HRA Analysis: ALL EYES ON BLING (9) was able to secure the perfect run behind the leader last time out in a stronger race and was able to finish it off well there running into second behind Eternal Bliss. She draws less favourably this time and can look to be running on late. IDEAL PURSUIT (2) was able to show good enough gate speed to work to the lead at Redcliffe and bounced back to form nicely leading all the way and winning by a big margin. She looks to find another race where she could lead and can look to lead all the way again. PROSPECTUS (1) secured a good run last time out behind Bracken Warrior and battled on well there for third in a race the winner rated good time. She draws well again in this race and should be right in the finish again. KING BLING (6) should be able to find a forward position in this race. He was forced to race without cover last time out and battled on well there for third. SELECTIONS: ALL EYES ON BLING (9), IDEAL PURSUIT (2), PROSPECTUS (1), KING BLING (6) SUGGESTED BET: IDEAL PURSUIT (2) to win.

DEGARMEA TEALE (2) looks to find a very suitable race where she may be able to work to the lead in the early stages. She sat without cover two starts ago and ran an excellent race there behind Ruggards Gee Tee. She should be hard to beat. MISTER SEASIDE (9) did a few things wrong in the score up but was able to hit the gate running before leading and handing over to Captain Jazz. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and looks to have strong place claims. RUBY RHAYNE BOW (3) has good gate speed and may be able to press forward and find the lead in the early stages of this race. She was seemingly a touch below her best last time out when sitting leaders back before fading late into fourth behind her smart stablemate Stripes. CRIPPA MAX (6) was a good winner two starts ago after sitting outside the leader and beating the smart horse Captain Jazz. He draws wide but has shown he is capable of doing work in his races and should run well again. SELECTIONS: DEGARMEA TEALE (2), MISTER SEASIDE (9), RUBY RHAYNE BOW (3), CRIPPA MAX (6) SUGGESTED BET: MISTER SEASIDE (9) to place.

PERFECT FEELING (2) has good gate speed and may be able to find the front in the early stages of this race. He was badly held up last time out before hitting the line nicely late for third at Redcliffe. ROSIE POLLEN (4) secured a good run close to the speed last time out and was just beaten by GALVARINO (9) who had raced on the pegs in the run. She should get a similar type of run in this race from a good draw and can be running on late again. MIGHTY IDEAL (10) got a long way back last time out at Redcliffe and ran on fairly late in a race taken out by Piccolo Diavolo. He may be shuffled back early again and can look to be running on late. SAINT LOUIS BEAT (1) has gate speed which gives him options in this race. He has seemingly been best in recent outings when driven with cover including two starts ago when finishing second to Diego Delgado. SELECTIONS: PERFECT FEELING (2), ROSIE POLLEN (4), MIGHTY IDEAL (10), SAINT LOUIS BEAT (1) SUGGESTED BET: PERFECT FEELING (2) to win.

BRACKEN WARRIOR (8) led last time out setting a strong tempo at this track and running a good second behind Miss Bay King Cole. He should get a good run through in this race behind a horse likely to be keen to hold a forward position and should run well from there. TAKE A CHANCE (9) found some trouble last time out at this track when starting favourite over the 2138 and took no competitive part there. He steps back to the mile which looks suitable and draws well enough. BONNIES CAM (4) has excellent early speed and should be able to find a forward position in this race. He has had a few runs back from a spell and seems to be building towards some of his better form which should see him very competitive in a race of this nature. KONNYMARA (1) has poor numerical form but does seemingly find a more suitable race and steps back to the mile which could be to his liking. He may be an improver in this race. SELECTIONS: BRACKEN WARRIOR (8), TAKE A CHANCE (9), BONNIES CAM (4), KONNYMARA (1) SUGGESTED BET: BRACKEN WARRIOR (8) to win.

SQUAMISH (6) was running on powerfully two starts ago and just couldn’t quite pick up the winner DARCYS FIREBALL (8) who was able to edge him out in the concluding stages. He draws to advantage over that horse this time and should be right in the finish again. DARCYS FIREBALL (8) was an excellent winner last time out at Redcliffe overcoming a 30 metre handicap to score there. He is racing in great form at the moment and despite the awkward inside back row draw he should run well again. NORTHERN HEIGHTS (7) got back last time out from a wide draw and was running on nicely late into fourth. He is a horse with good ability but doesn’t always bring his best manners which can let him down at times. NELLIE JOY (9) started off a 30 metre handicap last time out at Redcliffe and was running on nicely there into third behind stablemate DARCYS FIREBALLL (8). She looks likely to get a good run through and should be closing late again. SELECTIONS: SQUAMISH (6), DARCYS FIREBALL (8), NORTHERN HEIGHTS (7), NELLIE JOY (9) SUGGESTED BET: SQUAMISH (6) to win.

AMAMI (7) was able to lead all the way and score a good win at this track recently. He draws wide in this race but looks quite well placed in this field and should run well. O B LEGAL (3) was closing strongly two starts ago at this track when finishing third in good time behind Fifty Three Stars. He may be sat up and saved for one run over the 2138 and should be running into the finish late. SITTING ON EIGHT (1) has very good gate speed and should be able to lead early in this race. He is probably best suited over the 1660 but with the right run in this race he can run well. COMMODORE JUJON (6) ran on strongly last time out at Redcliffe in a race taken out by Buddy Perfect. He draws wide in this race but it is a small field and he should still be close enough. SELECTIONS: AMAMI (7), O B LEGAL (3), SITTING ON EIGHT (1), COMMODORE JUJON (6) SUGGESTED BET: O B LEGAL (3) each way.

HYPNOTIZE ME (2) showed good gate speed to lead last time out before handing over and was still running on late in a race taken out by Deal It Vinnie. He should be able to find a forward position in this race and should run well from there. DOUGS TRIBE (8) got shuffled a long way back last time out and was running on well there into fourth in a race taken out by Goodoldboysandbeer who has since run well again. He should get the right run and can be running on late again. VICTREE CHARLIE (4) isn’t a horse which possesses much gate speed which is likely to see him shuffled back early in this race. He got back in the run last time out and was running on well into fifth behind Vodka En Ice. TORO LOCO (5) was able to secure the perfect run behind the leader last time out before flashing late and just missing nabbing Im Busted. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: HYPNOTIZE ME (2), DOUGS TRIBE (8), VICTREE CHARLIE (4), TORO LOCO (5) SUGGESTED BET: HYPNOTIZE ME (2) to win.

BLACK VIPER (12) will start outside the 20m handicap due to being ODS. He sprinted up sharply last time out and was impressive there running over the top late. He meets a similar field and should run well again. DINGANE (8) has taken on stronger company in his past two outings and made a break last time out taking no competitive part as a result. He steps back into much more suitable company and should be able to find a position up on speed. BUSTER DAN (6) was a dominant winner two starts ago before having less luck last time out when forced to do the work outside the leader finishing third behind BLACK VIPER (12). If he can begin well and find a prominent position he should run well again. LAYDOWNLUNA (9) did a lot of work in the run two starts ago before finding the front and fading late into fourth. She was much better last time out when being sat up and saved for one run when finishing second. SELECTIONS: BLACK VIPER (12), DINGANE (8), BUSTER DAN (6), LAYDOWNLUNA (9) SUGGESTED BET: BLACK VIPER (12) to win. OVERVIEW:KYVALLEY REEVA (3) hadn’t done much of note prior to last start, but her performance in winning her maiden was hard to ignore. John Caldow jumped aboard, pushed her forward to lead and she continued to extend, putting a gap on the opposition and winning with something in hand in solid closing sectionals. She had been unruly prior to that, so proceed with caution, but a repeat will see her hard to beat. THE PASO DOBLE (6) broke through for a terrific and deserved maiden victory last time out, showing his customary early gate speed and putting a space on his rivals. Even though he’s drawn wide, his gate manners can negate that, allowing him to look for a forward position and take running down again. RIPPING RONALDO (4) creates interest first-up from a break considering he went out on a high with a solid win at Maryborough in July. No trial into this, but this is an astute stable, so monitor betting. WHISKEY DAWN (7) will appreciate this level compared to her last two starts in stronger company, where she wasn’t too far off the winners. She’s yet to place since her maiden victory at this track, but is going okay. The draw just means she will have to work at some stage. JINXED (2) is a 3yo filly having her second start and showed good speed for a sound fourth on debut last week. She can run well again based on that performance. BACK: KYVALLEY REEVA (3)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:KYVALLEY REEVA (3), THE PASO DOBLE (6), RIPPING RONALDO (4), WHISKEY DAWN (7)

OVERVIEW:WAR ZONE (10) was held up at a vital stage last week and may have gone close to winning had he seen daylight a little earlier, and they ran decent time for this grade. He was a winner three starts back, again in good time, when able to lead. Although the draw and map do him no favours, he can sweep home with the right tempo. JUSTLIKEDAVE (7) is a horse who never seems to have much luck with barrier draws and, as a result, is often turning in nice runs from difficult positions. He gets no favours again, but this doesn’t look as strong as what he’s been opposed to. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6) loomed up and was disappointing in the straight last time, and that was coming off a decent win at Shepparton. Herbertson will no doubt give him every chance to improve, so keep him safe. PICKLE IT (5) was disappointing last week, but that was a slightly harder race. He does run his best races when able to find the front, so he may be open to improvement. The chances don’t end there, with a case able to be made for most in the race, headed by MIKI MARK (4) and POWERLINC (3), who also go in the Early Quaddie. SELECTIONS:WAR ZONE (10), JUSTLIKEDAVE (7), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6), PICKLE IT (5)

OVERVIEW: Incredibly challenging race and hard to be confident. BETTA THAN LOVE (3) has been well supported in his two runs since returning to Victoria. He had his chance two starts back when second, then tried to lead last time but was under pressure a lap out and was beaten by a space. The stewards’ report had enough detail to suggest there may have been excuses, and he could bounce back off that effort. Monitor betting for any added confidence. HOME AND DRY (9) hasn’t won since March, when he was able to lead, but you can make a case that this race looks to be his most suitable in some time. The form of this field suggests they are unlikely to be running fast times, which might be more comfortable for his sweet spot. He has a soft trailing draw to conserve and come with one run. CHASING THE WIND (4) worked mid-race here last week and was sound to the line in a slogging affair. He hasn’t won in well over a year, but Alford jumps on again, so he’s worth considering. DELTA STARZ (6) was a winner two starts back, although the form out of that race hasn’t necessarily stacked up. He has an in-form driver, which helps. I had ROCKROLL RAMBO (7) on top from the same draw last week and he was never a factor, working home fairly. He will likely be map-negative again, so has place claims, similar to REASON TO LAUGH (10), who will need the right tempo. SELECTIONS:BETTA THAN LOVE (3), HOME AND DRY (9), CHASING THE WIND (4), DELTA STARZ (6)

OVERVIEW:ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (3) is returning to more suitable grade after performing well in the VICBRED Series, where she ran home well without much luck in the final. There’s a form reference from Maryborough four starts back, where she was able to lead and was run down on the post by MONTANA PRIDE (4), who she meets here with a better draw. The stable is worth respecting as infrequent visitors to Cranbourne. MONTANA PRIDE (4) is racing very well, and his three runs at Melton since the race where they met have all been very good, with not much going his way on each occasion. He’s the testing material. KOSIMO (9) seems well suited with his claiming price dropping him significantly in class. Although he was poor last time, his runs haven’t been too bad at Melton and he was a winner there in May in much tougher grade. UBETTA KNOT (1) has been a little costly her past couple, but she has either had to work or had a tricky draw, and gets a much easier map this time. If they overcook things in front, she should get her chance along the sprint lane. PLATINUM JIVE (5) is a very nice mare who’s been freshened for this off a trial win at Bacchus Marsh. She has a very good record at this track and can sprint well off a helmet. She just has a sticky draw and will need the right tempo. SELECTIONS:ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (3), MONTANA PRIDE (4), KOSIMO (9), UBETTA KNOT (1)

OVERVIEW: MASTER LOUEY (5) was found on top from a soft pole draw here last week and ran well, just unable to sprint down the winner in a solid last half. This is a big drop in quality from what he faced last week and, now fitter fourth-up, he should be primed to put his best foot forward. You get the leading driver to navigate a sticky draw and give him every chance to be too strong for his rivals late in what looks a very suitable race. JUST PEDRO (8) looks to get the cosy run behind the likely leader here and conserve for one run late. He was a good winner last time at Ballarat and isn’t disadvantaged here being an ODM runner. OUR PINUP GIRL (6) was disappointing last week, but she was first-up and the market suggested she may need the outing. The stable goes well at this track and she’s worth another chance. BONA KHAN (1) will look to lead here, as he so often likes to do from these draws, and has been going okay. He just prefers the shorter distances, and seeing out this trip strongly is the concern. ILLAWONG PHOENIX (7) is going okay for the new stable but has a tricky draw to overcome and, although he will need luck, has solid claims at the minor end. BACK: MASTER LOUEY (5)– 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: MASTER LOUEY (5), JUST PEDRO (8), OUR PINUP GIRL (6), ILLAWONG PHOENIX (7)

OVERVIEW: LE GASTON (3) based on his SP profile alone, will start a short-priced favourite here, and on the strength of his first-up victory he deserves to head the market. He has overall been costly to punters, didn’t win by much at Kilmore, and the time wasn’t overly flash. He has a stable and driver in form and strikes a winnable race here. He’s not a “chips in” job at this stage, however. EAGLEYE (6) brings different form from NSW, where she was a last-start winner at Newcastle in decent time. More significantly, she joins a stable that has an excellent strike rate with horses new to the yard and often gets an upsurge in what they are able to produce. Watch the betting and include her in the Quaddie. MATRIARCH DAISY (5) is a 3yo filly who was in terrific form, but her last two runs have been well short of what she is capable of. She’s a go-forward type and her best form can win this, so keep her safe. STORM VENDETTA (4) was okay here last week in running second from a soft draw and is worth keeping safe again, as he should map okay. SELECTIONS: LE GASTON (3), EAGLEYE (6), MATRIARCH DAISY (5), STORM VENDETTA (4)

OVERVIEW:MAJESTIC CHARMA (8) finds a very suitable race with the mare’s allowance, being the sole runner off the back row and likely to map closer than she did last time out, when she rattled to the line in a slick closing section in a bigger and stronger field. She can tend to be a bit dicey at the start, but if she fills her action well, in this grade you can expect her to storm home late. JOU LOU (4) will no doubt be popular in the market on the back of winning four from six and developing a nice partnership with James Herbertson. He musters good gate speed and will look for the top end over the short trip, where he won last time. His times, however, haven’t been overly strong in weaker company, so although he ticks a lot of boxes, he does strike a better grade. BERTINELLI (7) is an interesting runner from NSW, where he hasn’t won in nearly a year but has been performing okay against largely Tuesday Menangle grade. He has a tricky draw to overcome but warrants respect. RIGHT OF REPLY (3) had every chance here and couldn’t sprint with them, but this does look a little more suitable and he should map well again. There are a number in the mix for the minor prize, including ATEGO DAWN (1), STEADY DREAM (2) and CARTALCHA (6). BACK: MAJESTIC CHARMA (8)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJESTIC CHARMA (8), JOU LOU (4), BERTINELLI (7), RIGHT OF REPLY (3)

OVERVIEW: UNCLE BILL (6) stands out here based on his maiden performance, where he showed good gate speed before taking cover and holding his ground against an above-average type who subsequently made the VICBRED Final. The exposed form of the others has been untrustworthy, so although you need to apply some caution with maiden trotters, this one is showing more positivity than the opposition. ALECTRONA (1) is getting closer to a win based on her past few performances and looks to map well here from the soft draw. Her times are comparable with the top pick and she can go close. ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8) has a solid SP profile but came through the same race as the top pick last time out and galloped in running, although he was dropping out prior. He’s a great looker and can improve if the penny drops. CASUAL CONNECTION (4) is a NSW visitor from a strong stable who’s only had the one run, where she broke three times in running. She’s had plenty of trials, but the penny is yet to drop. She goes in merely out of respect for the stable, as she’s yet to command confidence based on performance. BACK: UNCLE BILL (6)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:UNCLE BILL (6), ALECTRONA (1), ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8), CASUAL CONNECTION (4)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY STRANGER (4) is a 2yo taking on older horses here, but he did so last time out when able to win his maiden at Terang after getting a perfect trip behind the leader. I’m not sure how strong that form is, but he will be better for the outing. It’s also unclear exactly how he maps here, but he will no doubt be popular in the market given the respect the stable commands in a race of this nature. CARUSO STAR (6) looks well suited as an 11-time winner, whereas many of the opposition have only won their maiden. He’s fitter now fourth-up and, more importantly, goes to the front row and has a draw to use his gate speed. He beat a better field two starts back here when mapping softly. QUICK CRUNCH (5) is a fast beginner and has been racing consistently overall this season. She was a winner five starts back when able to lead and control before just scraping home. Since then, she either hasn’t had the right draws or set-ups but has still been sound. She’s a winner at this track and, if she finds the top, will take running down. OPERTSER (1) was a winner two starts back, beating CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7), with both driven to run on and performing well. They’ve both placed again since and must be given claims in a race with different form lines to assess. SELECTIONS:JILLIBY STRANGER (4), CARUSO STAR (6), QUICK CRUNCH (5), OPERTSER (1)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG MARICRUZ (4) is a horse you will be able to get a strong line on, as she ran second to the top pick in the previous race last time at Terang, where she led and had every chance but was okay. If JILLIBY STRANGER happens to do the job in the previous race, her stocks will rise. Aside from that, the time she ran there may be good enough to get the job done this time, and with a smart stable behind her and tactical speed, she’s the starting point. RIDE HIGH CAPTAIN (2) is open to sharp improvement in his numerical form after a sound fifth here last week in a stronger race, and prior to that stuck on okay for second when sitting parked. He may map to get the right run and get his chance late. KING BALDWIN (6) has only had the one trial for the new stable, which was sound, and now makes his debut after plenty of experience at the trials in NSW. He’s hard to get a line on, but the trainer/driver combination warrants respect. MEGALODON (1) is another first starter who’s been at the Bacchus Marsh trials, which are inconclusive, but he is a market watch from the soft draw. SELECTIONS:KEAYANG MARICRUZ (4), RIDE HIGH CAPTAIN (2), KING BALDWIN (6), MEGALODON (1)

A small field for the two-year-olds opens the night and is extremely hard to assess. RYHAD (1) showed good speed to lead on debut before tiring late after producing a nice trial prior. Expect he may attempt similar tactics here and should be further improved from the race-day experience. HEZA PINUP BOY (3) is the other Todd Rattray-trained runner and has been competitive in a couple of fast-run races thus far in his career. It's unlikely they will run those sorts of times in this field, so he should be more than competitive. SOLO SNITCH (2) has been competing in the feature races of late and earning cheques, as has ILLWONG KAMISORI (5), so it wouldn't surprise to see either of them bob up and win here. SKIPPING VINNIE (4) is on debut and finished second in a trial around a month ago, albeit beaten a fair distance, so the market may be the best guide to his chances. Selections:HEZA PINUP BOY (3), RYHAD (1), SOLO SNITCH (2), ILLWONG KAMISORI (5)

QUARTIERA (2) was super impressive on debut, coming from well back to record a 22-metre victory in nice time. This is no doubt a rise in class, but he looks to have plenty of ability, so it wouldn't surprise to see him put another victory next to his name. MAXX (3) won in a very fast mile first up in the state after arriving from the Riverina and should find himself on speed again here, giving him every chance. Expect SPORTZSILK (4) to also put itself into the race early with its natural gate speed, noting it has undergone a stable change since its last start. ARDEN SEASCAPE (8) is first up in nearly 12 months for visiting trainer Dean Braun. She looks an extremely classy filly at her best and has had numerous trials to prepare for her return. She strikes a very awkward draw, but with clear running her class may shine through. ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (9) is another first up in the state after arriving from the Riverina and, barring his past few efforts, his prior form was very good and would see him right in the finish here. REMMINGTON (11) and PHLOW JO (6) look the best of the rest from their awkward draws. Selections:QUARTEIRA (2), ARDEN SEASCAPE (8), MAXX (3), ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (9)

There looks to be good early speed here over the mile distance from the front row, headed by MIRA DOMINA (3), who was disappointing from the pole last start but had produced two strong performances prior. If she brings her best and finds the pegs, she would have to be a strong chance again. JUST LIKA DREAM (6) put together a string of strong performances last preparation before suffering interference first up two weeks ago. Expect she may roll forward from the wide draw here. Tactics will be interesting with SWEET DIXIE (7) from the outside of the front row, but it wouldn't surprise to see connections press forward over the shorter distance this week after restraining last start. KEAYANG LEXI (1) again draws a nice gate and should get every opportunity to earn another cheque for connections. The veterans JEREMY WELLS (11) and GOBSMACKED (12) will be relying on a hard tempo up front to bring them into the race late, although they may struggle over the short distance as they did last start. Selections:JUST LIKA DREAM (6), SWEET DIXIE (7), MIRA DOMINA (3), KEAYANG LEXI (1)

A standing-start event for the 50+ raters, with not a lot of winning form among the runners in recent starts. DONE WELL (6) can be hit and miss from the stand, but if she steps cleanly from the front row, with no noted sharp beginners around her, she could be the one at value first up from a break. REPETITIVE (5) wasn't far away at previous starts in similar fields and should find herself on speed with a good beginning. KNOCK OUT (1) gets his chance to return to the podium after striking awkward draws of late. SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (7) can never be discounted in races of this nature, and his usual quick beginning should see him find a nice position on speed with cover, allowing him every chance to be in the finish. ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (9) is clearly the class runner of the field but faces an extremely tough task from the 30-metre handicap over the middle distance. His chances may rely on several of those in front of him beginning tardily. Selections:DONE WELL (6), SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (7), ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (9), REPETITIVE (5)

TALK IS CHEAP (3) should have enough speed to find the pegs here and take plenty of running down, with her best racing generally coming when able to dictate terms in front. There doesn't appear to be a whole lot of pressure from the outside of the front row early or throughout the race, unless KIAVINO STRIDE (8) is put into the race as the lone back-row runner. Happy to forgive KUHUO KREST (7) for his last-start effort when doing the work outside the leader, which isn't his preferred racing pattern, and expect him to be running home strongly again here in the small field. ROSE NOIRE (4) produced an improved effort last start, while NO NUKES SKIPPER (6) and ALBY PRIDDY (5) look the best of the rest in what is an extremely even field. Selections:TALK IS CHEAP (3), KUHIO KREST (7), ROSE NOIRE (4), NO NUKES SKIPPER (6)

At his best, ZEUS IMMORTAL (2) would be expected to go close to winning here. He competed well in the four-year-old Sires before being thereabouts in races of late, and should find himself on speed with cover and get his chance to return to the winner's circle. MIGHT AND TEMERITY (3) may attempt to cross to the pegs here as he did last start when getting another win next to her name. She again uses the double claim to gain entry into this race and should be thereabouts in the finish. POST KEG (1) gets the pole draw and should receive every opportunity if the gaps appear late, should he be unable to hold the front, and is rarely far away in races of this nature. SHOOBEES SPIRIT (6) and CHAMONIX may be relying on some tempo to develop through the middle stages to allow them to get into the finish late. Selections:ZEUS IMMORTAL (2), MIGHT AND TEMERITY (3), POST KEG (1), SHOOBEES SPIRIT (6)

Another small field rounds out the night in the lowest class-rated race over the mile distance, where BARBETTE (1) and FEELINKINDALUCKY (2) both possess good gate speed and have been consistent in this grade of late, making them the leading hopes. SWEET AMOUR (4) is first up for the new stable and, if she brings her best form, could simply be too strong for this opposition. QUEENOFDANCE (6) loves bobbing up at big odds in races of this nature and can't be ruled out, while STAROFREMEMBRANCE (5) and EMER (3) have been racing a little below their best of late, but it wouldn't surprise to see either loom as a winning chance in a race like this. Selections:BARBETTE (1), FEELINKINDALUCKY (2), SWEET AMOUR (4), QUEENOFDANCE (6) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

TWIN CONNECTION (1) was a winner by 7.9 metres last start at Globe Derby when he defeated PARISIAN BANDIT. He should find the lead from gate one tonight and lead all of the way. KEILAH (8) is well drawn and she should get a nice run into the race behind the leader from the second row. PARISIAN BANDIT (5) and TRIGGER (10) are also chances.

DHAULAGIRI (7) was extremely disappointing last start at Globe Derby but then he returned to the winners list five starts after that at Mildura. If he can repeat his Mildura form he should be hard to beat. LAST TANGO IN HEAVEN (1), HEZROCKINROYALTY (2) and OUR INDIFFERENCE (6) are also chances.

KETO (6) ran a very nice race first up behind HEEZ A VIBE last start. If he can get over and find the lead he will be very hard to beat. He is a strong chance after that impressive run last start. FLY THE BANNER (10), HEEZ A VIBE (7) and DEE JAYS MISS (5) are all big chances in what is a very even race.

HEZ SO ROYAL (3) has won two of his last three starts and he defeated IM ALL BUSINESS by 2.7 meters last start and attacked the line for a classy win. He looks extremely hard to beat tonight. LOCHINVAR LEADER (7) won’t like the draw but he stands out as a major chance in a race like this. NOTGUILTY (6) and B T CAPTIVATE (1) are also chances.

SOUTH AUSSIE STAR (8) returns from a few months off. She ran a handy trial here at Globe Derby recently. She will need some luck but she will be right in the finish if she gets a clear run. KOJAX (3) brings some strong NSW form into this race. It may pay to watch his market moves tonight. CECIL PEAK (4) and JADES REASON (1) are also chances.

HARRO HILL (7) was disappointing last start but her runs previous two starts were very impressive. If she can bring her best form tonight she will be very hard to beat. REACH THE PEAK (3) is first up from a spell. His form at Globe Derby last preparation was strong and he looks like a threat tonight despite not being seen at the trials. PER ARDUA AD ASTRA (1) will love the inside draw and is a big threat. TONKAWAIKON (6) is always a sneaky chance in a race like this.

VATICAN GREEN (6) finds his sort of race tonight. He either wins or runs towards the tail of the field. He can storm home and he is a major chance tonight. KITTYKAT CUTIE (2) finds an easier race tonight compared to her last two outings. She is well drawn and is a strong chance of leading all of the way but her last two runs are a minor concern. SPLASH OF PAYNT (8) and MISS OUT (11) are also chances.

CHILDERS ROAD (8) defeated MEET ME AT THE BEACH by 3 metres last start. He is a major chance tonight if he can get a clear run and he has a tremendous strike rate for Ryan Hryhorec. STAR OF WILLOUGHBY (1), ASHANTE PRINCE (7) and ALLORNOTHINGLEVI (10) are also chances.

AMIRA MARIE (6) ran second behind SPLASH OF PAYNT last start and she is showing sings of wanting to win again. She is a big chance tonight. PERFECT GAMBLE (2), TREACHEROUS ROCK (1) and LONESTAR WARRIOR (9) are also chances.

MAJESTIC SUMMER (2) will be a big danger off the front mark after an impressive last start win. She will be hard to beat if she steps away cleanly. REOFFENDER (8) has won three of his last five starts. He defeated HAYOAK by 6.6 meters. He will be a big threat tonight despite the tricky handicap. DAISY BOUCHEA (4) and CARLA PIXIE (7) are also chances. Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: LIBERTY STAR DUST (9) competed through the heats of the Vicbred Super Series at his latest start, and while well beaten, he certainly wasn’t disgraced in hot company. Before that, he won decisively at Kilmore after an eye-catching first-up run from the tail of the field at Melton. He draws well here on the second line and looks a progressive horse for Jodi Quinlan. Should run well. NINEDOLLA TOASTIE (3) has fought out the finish in her two runs since resuming in this grade and should run a forward race once again, the veteran LENARD ESS (5) has won his last two in dominant fashion in easier races than this but is clearly in good form, while CITY ROCKSTAR (8) draws to follow out the potential early leader in FIRESIDE (1) and her runner-up placing to Mount Barker Boy at Ballarat back in mid-July reads well for this. She has had excuses her past two and might be a good roughie. Most of the others have claims in a race where not many would surprise. BACK: LIBERTY STAR DUST (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: LIBERTY STAR DUST (9), NINEDOLLA TOASTIE (3), LENARD ESS (5), CITY ROCKSTAR (8)

OVERVIEW: SEA FURY (3) won his trial at Shepparton in preparation for this first-up assignment and returns following a string of placings to close his most recent campaign. He ran good races for second to nice types such as Odin, Hitch To His Star and Intrusion before a break, with his last win being in the Wangaratta Pacing Cup during March. There’s some speed to his outside here, but if he’s able to work forward and wrestle the front, he’d prove hard to run down. He doesn’t win out of turn, but I’m a big fan of GUNFORHIRE (9) and his last two starts have been fast-finishing runner-up placings. He’s very talented and can certainly prevail with the right trip, with the small field set to suit his run-on style. FERRIGNO (8) draws inside the back row and hasn’t been far away in recent starts, nor has RANGER RICK (4), who looks another of the gate speed runners off the front. He had a softer trip than GUNFORHIRE (9) last start at Terang, but was easily beaten home into third. KEAYANG PAYTON (5) and OH SWEET CREATURE (2) look next best. SELECTIONS: SEA FURY (3), GUNFORHIRE (9), FERRIGNO (8), RANGER RICK (4)

OVERVIEW: Concerned about getting crossed and buried away at the start here with RUBYS DREAM (1), but going with her on top first-up for the powerhouse Lee stable. Her two trials since joining the camp have been good, with a win over stablemate KEAYANG LAVITA (6) and a close-up third to pacer Sweetheart Bart and top trotter Hoppy. Looks to be going well and just needs to hold a prominent position from one to be a key winning hope. Stablemate KEAYANG LAVITA (6) overcame a 20m handicap to win narrowly first-up from a break and is very talented when she does it all right, ALDEBARAN SUSANNE (2) has good gate speed and becomes a winning factor if she gets to the fence like she did when scoring narrowly last time out at Melton, while DICHOTOMY (9) has cost herself with gallops her past two, but a faultless display would have her right in this. THUNDA STRUCK (3) also flies the gate and while his first-up fifth was just fair, he’s a factor along with a few others headed by KEAYANG GYPSY (8). BACK: RUBYS DREAM (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RUBYS DREAM (1), KEAYANG LAVITA (6), ALDEBARAN SUSANNE (2), DICHOTOMY (9)

OVERVIEW: ZANDA MAN (7) finished last campaign with a string of good efforts in strong company, including a couple of Saturday night wins at Melton. He returned from a break with a midfield finish in a heat of the Vicbred Super Series at Kilmore late last month, and while well beaten, it was a nice effort from off the fence. The draw is sticky, but he’s quite progressive and might be the class runner in this clash. CAPTAIN PINS (8) returned from a spell with a big win at Charlton and another good closing effort from last for sixth at Melton, while WHERE IS WOODY (1) was a great winner from three back the fence last time at Maryborough and might land a position closer here behind likely early leader PISTOL PEARCE (2), who was a bit outclassed last time but had been running well prior and maps for a good trip. Others to consider are ISOLATION (4), who trialled well for his return with a soft recent win at Melton, and TARA VICTORY (6), who won an easier race at Shepparton on September 1. SELECTIONS: ZANDA MAN (7), CAPTAIN PINS (8), WHERE IS WOODY (1), PISTOL PEARCE (2)

OVERVIEW: SOHO DARKNSTORMY (7) is the key runner and form reference in a great little race to start the main Quaddie. He led from this draw over the 2240m at Melton on August 22 and was beaten home into fourth by PESCI (6), GOOD TOBE LOCKSLEY (4) and CLYMENUS (2) who all reoppose. Last time out, over the 1720m trip, he led again and actually held on to beat HITTHEROADJACK (1), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (3), PESCI (6) and ATA RANGI (5). So what happens here? Well, you’d assume he leads again and gives a great sight, but perhaps gets tired in the concluding stages and gives his rivals a chance. Given it’s over the middle trip again, I’ll side with HITTHEROADJACK (1), who is one-paced but going well and draws for a great trip on the fence. GOOD TOBE LOCKSLEY (4) charged late from three back the fence for second behind PESCI (6) last time, while CLYMENUS (2) rarely runs a bad race and needs things to go his way, but is a winning factor. SELECTIONS: HITTHEROADJACK (1), SOHO DARKNSTORMY (7), GOOD TOBE LOCKSLEY (4), CLYMENUS (2)

OVERVIEW: MY UNCLE STAN (7) was held up badly and absolutely rocketed late when fourth, beaten just 4.2m, behind Ollies The Boss at Melton on August 29 in what was the run of a coming winner. You can excuse his start prior when he galloped out of play, and his effort before that when burning early, finding the front and boxing on for second to the smart I Am The Storm was also very good in a fast mile rate of 1:52.3. Small field suits and he’s going good enough to run over the top here. Big fan of the mare MITZI SAID (1), who could have finished even closer than her 6m fourth first-up at Melton with more luck. She had no chance from out the back in a fast last quarter at Wagga latest, and she can win from gate one if she’s not buried away too far. IMA TERMINTOR (2) can be a player if he crosses to the fence as expected, BLAKE BOLAC (6) was a good second to New Shuffle at the trials ahead of this first-up assignment and is a handy type, ALL BLAZING GUNS (4) is poking along alright at present and can figure with the right trip, while PLAINS IN HEAVEN (3) finished midfield in a Victoria Cup this time last year and a return to that form is obviously good enough. BACK: MY UNCLE STAN (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MY UNCLE STAN (7), MITZI SAID (1), IMA TERMINTOR (2), BLAKE BOLAC (6)

OVERVIEW: If you are a regular backer of SPIRITED LASS (5) then she’s probably given you a couple of grey hairs, but also plenty of thrills along the way. She’s talented, but her manners are very dicey as evidenced by her past couple of starts when she’s galloped in the run. Scott Ewen’s mare loomed to win last weekend as a $1.45 favourite at Cranbourne but went off stride, and before that just couldn’t find clear running and ultimately went up in the air when well fancied in a good race on a Saturday night. If she trots here, I think she wins. FLYIN TIME (3) hasn’t won yet this campaign, but is knocking on the door and heads here after a runner-up placing at Kilmore when she kicked clear at the corner before being hauled in by Aldebaran Denbay. There was a big margin back to third there and she looks the potential early leader. Key danger. AGAINST THE BRIDLE (6) has won his past two in easier grade with the master James Herbertson aboard, while WHY NOW (4) broke his maiden in good style at start three last week at Ballarat and should run a forward race. BACK: SPIRITED LASS (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: SPIRITED LASS (5), FLYIN TIME (3), AGAINST THE BRIDLE (6), WHY NOW (4)

OVERVIEW: Very even looking contest, but fancy SCAR (5) is running the best of these at present and I’ll lean his way in a wide-open contest for the 57-67 rated trotters. He sat parked last start and looked in trouble at the corner, but dug deep to beat QUEEN KIZEN (2) and co. at Kilmore. He was very brave in a couple of runs from the chair prior to that, and was beaten just 3.7m by Hallebesofine at his last appearance at Geelong. That horse is well fancied in a Group 1 Vicbred final on Saturday night. Reads well. TICTOK (1) is going along okay and draws well in a race where she is expected to lead or be leader’s back. Last weekend at Melton, she sat in the one-one and managed to finish third to Vici Bloom. From the pole, she must be a chance. PARIS KAY (4) beat home TICTOK (1) last time out and did win a race of this grade from the front at Melton in mid-July, while RARITY ROCK (3) was a very good winner at Cranbourne two back before only a fair display last time at Geelong when settling well back in the running line. All of these can win with the right trip, so don’t be afraid to go wide in the last leg of the Quaddie. SELECTIONS: SCAR (5), TICTOK (1), PARIS KAY (4), RARITY ROCK (3) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R1 #9 LIBERTY STAR DUST – 2 units (win) R3 #1 RUBYS DREAM – 2 units (win) R6 #7 MY UNCLE STAN – 3 units (win) R7 #5 SPIRITED LASS – 3 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 3,5,9/3,4,5,8,9/1,2,6,8,9/1,7,8 QUADDIE 1,2,4,6,7/1,2,6,7/3,5,6/1,3,4,5 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: What a brilliant race this is to kick off the meeting at Kilmore. THE ART OF SUCCESS (9) is one of the most exciting mares in the country and she is aiming up for her ninth straight victory here. Most of her wins have come from in front, so her barrier makes for her to adopt a different racing pattern here. But regardless, she is a star and a horse to watch in the Vicbred Super Series Final next weekend. HOUSE PARTY (10) is the new mare on the scene. She’s a big horse and has been given time to develop. She hasn’t been seen since her dominant victory in the Encipher Stakes in October last year. She has only had the two career starts and we will learn more about her here. Fitness is a query. MIKI MOO (2) is a quality mare trained and driven by top NSW participant Luke McCarthy. She has spent most of her career racing in Brisbane. Her own sectional times aren’t far off the big guns in this field and she gets an ideal barrier. WICKED CONFESSION (8), the inaugural Running Of The Bulls winner, is all class and she’s won her two starts back this campaign in style, but she will need to overcome a sticky barrier. Also respecting Ladies In Red’s sister LUV THE NITELIFE (7) as well as PEACE OUT (11) in this event. BACK: R1 #9 THE ART OF SUCCESS into R3 #4 THE LAST TRIP – 3 units (win multi) SELECTIONS:THE ART OF SUCCESS (9), HOUSE PARTY (10), MIKI MOO (2), WICKED CONFESSION (8)

OVERVIEW: LET HER ROLL (5) is a talented mare. She has only raced three times this year, but as a juvenile she was one of the leading fillies in her age group. In her last start, the mile rate was 1.51.9 and she finished fifth but had to cover an extra 35 metres, racing wide from her tough barrier. Her class is there, but her barrier may be tricky with talented mares to her inside. SOAP AND BUBBLES (3) is a fast mare with terrific gate speed. She has the talented SOHO AMERICANO (2) drawn to her inside, but she may still try to cross early. If she can find the fence here, she looks a great chance. SHES ALLABOUTLUV (9) has been a dominant force in the Tasmanian ranks over the last year. She’s won 10 of 14 starts this season. She was run down by WICKED CONFESSION in a recent Kilmore trial. She is a quality mare, but this looks to be one of her toughest asks to date. SOHO AMERICANO (2) has been a star in her age group, racing her whole career. She won the QLD and VIC Oaks last year at the top level. She is a versatile mare but seems to be performing a little below her best. The good barrier here suits her well. Also, MISS ARI (8) is a runner that can’t be left out here with her brilliant turn of foot. SELECTIONS: LET HER ROLL (5), SOAP AND BUBBLES (3), SHES ALLABOUTLUV (9), SOHO AMERICANO (2)

OVERVIEW: THE LAST TRIP (4) couldn’t be more impressive in his four runs since returning to the racetrack this year. All four runs have been dominant victories with a combined winning margin of 90.9. Wow! This field is full of class and looks his toughest test. CIGANO (8) has only had the two starts this year and is first up since July. He’s a talented performer who is versatile and can be driven for his speed or strength, but he has an awkward barrier here and will need luck. SCHWARZ (5) has been unbeaten in his five runs this year, the most recent four all being in Tasmania. He’s in flying form, but this is harder. SAO PAULO SIMBA (9) won four of his last five starts at Menangle before going amiss last start. He’s raced at the top level his whole career and will get a good trip here from barrier nine to be flashing home late. COASTAL DRIVE (2), FORTY LOVE (3), FIRE MARSHALL (1) and STORMS COLLIDE (7) are all talented horses as well that can’t be left out here and look first four hopes. BACK: R1 #9 THE ART OF SUCCESS into R3 #4 THE LAST TRIP – 3 units (win multi) SELECTIONS:THE LAST TRIP (4), CIGANO (8), SCHWARZ (5), SAO PAULO SIMBA (9)

OVERVIEW: FOX DAN (1) is last year’s Victoria Derby winner and Eureka runner-up. This is a quality field, but barrier one really helps the star four-year-old here. FAIRPLAY (5) is in fantastic form, winning his four starts this year impressively. He may look to work forward here, but regardless, he’s one of the standout performers in this field. HESITATE (3) has brilliant point-to-point speed. If he gets a comfortable trip here, he will be storming to the line late. NEW SHUFFLE (9) will get a good trip here from barrier nine without having to be used up early. He looks a good first four hope. Also respecting APOLLOSTORM (10), HITCH TO HIS STAR (8) and CALEXICO (2) in this event. BACK: R4 #1 FOX DAN into R5 #8 I AM THE STORM – 3 units(win multi) SELECTIONS:FOX DAN (1), FAIRPLAY (5), HESITATE (3), NEW SHUFFLE (9).

OVERVIEW: This looks to be another great race full of quality talent. I AM THE STORM (8) was brave last start, sitting in the breeze at Melton and still prevailing to be too strong. However, that was not surprising as he’s a talented horse that seems to have reached new heights this year. The barrier is awkward for him here. ITS CONFIDENTIAL (4) has not been performing poorly recently by any means, but he’s been a little bit out of form numerically. He suits races run at an even tempo where the last quarter isn’t super quick. Recently, all his runs have had a final quarter that has probably been a bit quick for him from well back in the field to make up ground. He was the winner of this series as a three-year-old and is absolutely proven at this level. He’s a talented horse. PICK UP ELVIS (9) has been super in his last two runs behind THE LAST TRIP. Two starts ago, he flashed home from last and wasn’t far behind the star four-year-old. He should get a good trip here. SEATHESTARS (3) is first up here, but he was eye-catching beating a nice field of horses in a recent Melton trial. He has raced at the top level his whole career and he should be able to map well here from barrier three. An interesting horse to note in this field is MCMAYHEM (5). He has done all his racing in Tasmania and is first up here for Mitchell Frost. BACK: R4 #1 FOX DAN into R5 #8 I AM THE STORM – 3 units(win multi) SELECTIONS:I AM THE STORM (8), ITS CONFIDENTIAL (4), PICK UP ELVIS (9), SEATHESTARS (3).

OVERVIEW: SHEER ME (4) has had two starts since moving to Victoria for two fourths. He was checked and got well back in his first run at Ararat but hit the line well. Last start, he did it tough at Shepparton, racing in the breeze, but still ran home well and was only beaten 4.2 metres. He gets his chance here. DYGANALI (8) ran home well for third two starts back and led last start to narrowly get beaten late. If it can get some luck here from the barrier, it’s one of the winning chances in this field. PARINI (5) is a lightly raced performer from the Stephen O'Donoghue stable. He is first up since July and has been trialling OK. He could be an improver. MY MATE ACE (7) is first up since last year. Fitness may be a query from the barrier, but he was a consistent performer last year and didn’t look far off winning his maiden. Noting JAMALA KHAN (2) is first up here for trainer Malcolm Bull. BAC: SHEER ME (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:SHEER ME (4), DYGANALI (8), PARINI (5), MY MATE ACE (7)

OVERVIEW: Trainer Brad Angove has a good hand in this race with AFRICAN GALA (4) and BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (1). AFRICAN GALA (4) comes out of a heat in the Vicbred Super Series won by Munny The Munster. He finished seventh here but certainly didn’t disgrace himself. This is an easier race and he looks well placed. BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (1) backs up from a third at Maryborough on Monday when she ran home well. She has barrier one here and should get a good trip. BUCKLES FOR BERRY (3) was a good second at Ballarat last start behind Dreams Of Love. She is starting to figure out what racing is all about and is performing confidently. She has a good turn of foot. SPANISH RIZARDO (5) was racing well last preparation and is first up here. Fitness is a query, especially from the awkward barrier. SELECTIONS:AFRICAN GALA (4), BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (1), BUCKLES FOR BERRY (3), SPANISH RIZARDO (5)

OVERVIEW: JESSICAS STORY (7) is stepping out here for the 200th time. She had a tough run last start but still hit the line really well for third. Barrier seven isn’t ideal, but she can make her own luck. FLING IT RAINBOW (2) won two starts ago when leading early and taking a sit to get a perfect fence trip. He may adopt similar tactics here. The flashy grey KALARNEY PRINCE (1) has been racing OK this preparation and will get a good fence trip here. ALDEBARAN MARCUS (6) is a contender here if he finds some luck. BACK: JESSICAS STORY (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: JESSICAS STORY (7), FLING IT RAINBOW (2), KALARNEY PRINCE (1), ALDEBARAN MARCUS (6)

OVERVIEW: This is a very competitive event to end the meeting. MASSIF CENTRAL (6)’s usual racing tactic is to use his early speed to find the fence. He will look to adopt similar tactics here. I prefer him over the shorter trip which he has here. BET BET HOTSHOT (1) has been out of form recently but gets the chance to turn it around here with the perfect fence trip. MACHO MAORI (2) will need to bring his best here, but he has been racing well for his grade and is a first four chance here. LITTLE TEDEY (8) can get it wrong with his manners, but being the only horse on the back row, he has time and space to settle early. At his best, he is a winning chance. SELECTIONS: MASSIF CENTRAL (6), BET BET HOTSHOT (1), MACHO MAORI (2), MOONSHINE LOUIE (7) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2) has been a consistent performer and should be suited by the mile distance here. His chances would be enhanced significantly if SHEMEANSBUSINESS (1) decides to take a sit this week after disappointing when leading over the same distance last start, albeit in quick time. MERRYWOOD PAUL (6) gets into this race well with the claim and could be the improver if there is some genuine tempo throughout. The three Wayne Yole-trained runners, NATIONAL NEWS (3), CAN FEEL THE FURY (4) and JAMES CAGNEY (5), are likely to be saved for one run and will also be relying on some solid tempo throughout to allow them to finish over the top of the favoured runners. Selections:WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), SHEMEANSBUSINESS (1), MERRYWOOD PAUL (6), NATIONAL NEWS (3)

A competitive No More Than Four Wins event, where Victorian visitor VIVID DREAM (7) brings some handy form to the state. She has undergone a stable change since her last start and may have to settle towards the rear of the field, but she looks the class horse of the race and may simply be too quick for them up the home straight with a nice run in transit. I GOTTA GO (3) broke through for a deserved victory last start after being unlucky on numerous occasions prior and should have enough gate speed to be first to the pegs here. There doesn't appear to be a lot of mid-race pressure unless ITZBUDDHA (4) grabs hold and pulls, so he should get every chance to finish on the podium. ROCKY STRIDE (5) drops back in grade after performing well in feature races of late and made good ground in a sharp mile last start. He possesses a very quick finishing burst when asked and looks a strong chance here. OUR WILLOW (6) is a four-year-old mare who clearly has plenty of ability when right. Her form has tapered off of late, but a change of scenery to a new stable may be the spark she needs to recapture her best. TAPPY (2) broke through for her first victory in the state last start, producing some nice closing sectionals to score. He should secure a nice run on speed with cover and gets every chance to finish on the podium again. Selections:VIVID DREAM (7), I GOTTA GO (3), ROCKY STRIDE (5), TAPPY (2)

IDEN OLIVER (2) has been quite dominant in his past two victories, recording good time over the middle distance, and again draws to get a nice run on speed here, gaining entry with the claim for driver Grace Jones. He may cop some early pressure from the Geoff Smith-prepared pair LIKEABLE ROGUE (3) and IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (6), but he should still get his chance to find a position on speed and be right in the finish. Both of those stablemates have been racing consistently of late and are due to break through for another victory, with their chances enhanced if either can find the pegs. KENYA (8) draws an awkward inside back-row gate but should appreciate some genuine tempo throughout and will be dangerous if the gaps come his way. JET TO HEAVEN (1) has broken at both starts since arriving in the state but could be right in the finish if he brings his best manners from the pole draw. TULLAH GIRL (4) uses the double claim to gain entry into this race and, if able to find a nice run in transit, should be running home strongly. Selections:IDEN OLIVER (2), LIKEABLE ROGUE (3), IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (6), KENYA (8)

The only full field of the night is for the maidens over the mile, where the talented but erratic SHIBASAKI (11) resumes from a break. He trialled nicely a month ago and has since undergone a stable change, and if he brings his best behaviour, he could take some holding out late. IDEN MISS WORLD (4) could be the improver, as I have her finding the pegs with her good gate speed. She also trialled nicely in handy time two weeks ago, and that form would see her right in the finish here. LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (9) is always thereabouts in races of this nature and should get a nice run through from the back-row draw to be running home strongly again. ARRIVAL TIME (8) draws an awkward gate but produced a handy enough performance first up in the state after doing some work, and should be in the finish if the gaps come his way. Selections:SHIBASAKI (11), IDEN MISS WORLD (4), LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (9), ARRIVAL TIME (8)

WEONA EAGLE (1) has returned to form over her past two starts and gets the handy draw to have options from the gate here. Expect INTO THE HARKNESS (2) and MUZZAME MATE (3) to push forward from their draws, while MY WAY (5) and LETSGOBRO (7) may also press forward with their good gate speed. That could set the race up nicely for the back-row runners WE SALUTE YOU (9) and MOVESLIKEALADY (10) to be finishing over the top. Both have been racing in good form of late and just need a nice run in transit to be strong winning chances here. JOHN VINCENT (6) would be expected to be driven with a sit and is another who could be finishing home strongly if he can get a nice cart into the race. Selections:WE SALUTE YOU (9), MOVESLIKEALADY (10), WEONA EAGLE (1), MUZZAMEMATE (3)

There looks to be a stack of speed here over the short-course distance, led by LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) and WAVES OF CHANCE (6) from the middle front-row draws. WAVES OF CHANCE (6) clearly has plenty of ability and, if he can find the pegs and settle in running, could take plenty of running down. ANOTHER NIEN (8) should be a beneficiary of the hot speed throughout and, as the lone back-row runner following the scratching of the expected favourite, should be able to work into the running line and finish home strongly late. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2) broke a long run of outs to score last start, hitting the line well, and looks set to receive another nice run on speed with cover here, giving him every chance to record back-to-back victories. Selections:ANOTHER NIEN (8), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2), WAVES OF CHANCE (6), CENTURIAN MISS (1)

The Free For All is an intriguing race, with the speed map likely to depend on whether PARDOE PLUGGA (5) and WATERMELON SUGAR (6) use their brilliant gate speed to attempt to find the pegs first. BETTABLACK TIGER (2) was good first up for the new stable and expect he may be driven more conservatively here from the nice draw after being from the pole last start. He should take plenty of beating with clear running. CUSTOM HARLEY (4) would be expected to be put into the race at some stage and is always thereabouts in the finish in races of this nature, while GO THE RED (8) will be relying on some solid tempo up front to allow him to finish home strongly, as he has done numerous times of late since arriving in the state. Selections:BETTABLACK TIGER (2), CUSTOM HARLEY (4), GO THE RED (8), WATERMELON SUGAR (6)

The low-class race rounds out the night, where there looks to be a bit of speed engaged from the front row. KYRGIOS (1) makes his first start for the Brent Parish stable and looks to have sufficient gate speed to hold a forward position. His mainland form prior to arriving in Tasmania has to be respected in a race of this nature. DANCINWIVJOLENE (2) is also first up from a break and gets a nice draw to kick-start her campaign, having been super competitive in races of this grade previously. MIDNITE DESIRE (4) was well fancied in the market at both starts after arriving interstate but was only fair despite receiving nice runs in transit. He has since had a let-up, so an improved effort wouldn't surprise, although the market may be the best guide. OUR SWEET TRIXIE (5) is always earning cheques but strikes an awkward draw, as does CHRIS BE QUICK (9), who loves filling a placing in races of this nature. MODERN JIVE (8) resumes from a let-up and could be the one at odds if he can secure a soft run along the pegs and the gaps appear late.
